question: Which State launched India' first PPP green waste processing plant? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Chhattisgarh
Madhya Pradesh
Kerala
Telangana
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Madhya Pradesh

Explanation:
India's first PPP (Public-Private Partnership) green waste processing plant has been established in Narmadapuram district of Madhya Pradesh. This plant will process green waste and convert it into useful products like compost, biogas, etc. The objective of this project is to efficiently dispose of green waste generated in urban areas and reduce environmental pollution. Under the PPP model, the government and a private company will jointly operate this plant. This initiative will help achieve the Swachh Bharat Mission and Sustainable Development Goals.

☛ Main objective of this plant → Processing of green waste and energy production

question_hi: किस राज्य ने भारत का पहला पीपीपी ग्रीन वेस्ट प्रोसेसिंग प्लांट लॉन्च किया? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)

Explanation:

question: The commercialisation of agriculture under the British transformed the rural economy. What did 'commercialisation of agriculture' in British India lead to? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (02/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Elimination of rural debt
Growth of self-sufficient villages
Rise in food grain production
Increased production of cash crops
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Increased production of cash crops

Explanation:
Under British rule, the commercialisation of agriculture primarily aimed at boosting production of cash crops (like cotton, indigo, tea, jute) for export and British industries. British policies compelled farmers to grow cash crops instead of food grains, leading to a decline in food security and an increase in rural indebtedness, not its elimination. Villages lost self-sufficiency and became dependent on markets. Food grain production fell because land was diverted to cash crops. Thus, the correct answer is Increased production of cash crops.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Primary reason for commercialisation → To supply raw materials for British industries
☛ Major cash crops → Cotton, indigo, tea, jute, opium
☛ Impact on food grain production → Declined, leading to famines
☛ Impact on rural debt → Increased, peasants fell into debt traps
☛ Social consequence → Self-sufficient villages ended, market dependence grew

question: What was the main characteristic of the Indian economy at the time of independence in 1947? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: High per capita income
Self-sufficiency in food grains
Dominance of the industrial sector
Predominantly agrarian with low productivity
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Predominantly agrarian with low productivity

Explanation:
At the time of independence in 1947, the Indian economy was predominantly agrarian, with about 75% of the population dependent on agriculture. Agriculture contributed around 50% of the Gross Domestic Product. However, productivity was very low due to outdated technology, inadequate irrigation, and exploitative land tenure systems. The industrial sector was underdeveloped, consisting mainly of textiles and sugar industries. Per capita income was very low, and the country faced a shortage of food grains, relying on imports. Thus, the economy was characterized by a backward agricultural sector with low productivity.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Population dependent on agriculture in 1947 → about 75%
☛ Agriculture's contribution to GDP at independence → about 50%
☛ State of Indian industries → underdeveloped, mainly cotton textiles and jute
☛ Per capita income → very low
☛ Food grain situation → dependent on imports

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है मुख्य रूप से कम उत्पादकता के साथ कृषि प्रधान

Explanation:
1947 में स्वतंत्रता के समय भारतीय अर्थव्यवस्था मुख्य रूप से कृषि प्रधान थी, जिसमें लगभग 75% जनसंख्या कृषि पर निर्भर थी। कृषि का सकल घरेलू उत्पाद में लगभग 50% योगदान था। हालांकि, उत्पादकता बहुत कम थी क्योंकि तकनीक पुरानी थी, सिंचाई सुविधाएं अपर्याप्त थीं, और भूमि व्यवस्था शोषणकारी थी। औद्योगिक क्षेत्र अविकसित था, जिसमें मुख्य रूप से कपड़ा और चीनी जैसे उद्योग थे। प्रति व्यक्ति आय बहुत कम थी और देश खाद्यान्न की कमी से जूझ रहा था।

question: In which of the following years was the Central Goods and Services Tax Act enacted? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: 2007
2013
2009
2017
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 2017

Explanation:
The Central Goods and Services Tax Act (CGST Act) was enacted by the Indian Parliament on 29 March 2017. It is a crucial part of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime in India, which came into effect on 1 July 2017. The CGST Act governs the tax levied by the central government on the supply of goods and services within a state. Along with this, the State GST (SGST) and Integrated GST (IGST) Acts were also passed. The CGST Act subsumed central excise duty, service tax, and several other indirect taxes. Under this Act, five tax slabs were fixed: 0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ When was the CGST Act enacted? → 29 March 2017
☛ When did GST become effective? → 1 July 2017
☛ Full form of CGST? → Central Goods and Services Tax Act
☛ When was the GST Council formed? → 15 September 2016
☛ How many tax slabs in GST? → Five (0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%)

question: What does globalisation mainly mean in economic terms? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Closing borders
Connecting to the world economy
Limiting trade
Stopping foreign investment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Connecting to the world economy

Explanation:
Economic globalisation refers to the integration of national economies through the free flow of goods, services, capital, technology, and labour across borders. It reduces trade barriers and encourages foreign investment, leading to increased interdependence among countries. This process fosters global supply chains, boosts foreign direct investment (FDI), and expands the role of multinational corporations (MNCs). Developing nations gain access to advanced technology and larger markets, while developed countries benefit from cheaper resources and labour. Globalisation also promotes competition, innovation, and economic growth. Thus, it is the opposite of closing borders or limiting trade; instead, it emphasises connecting to the world economy through international economic cooperation.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Main economic meaning of globalisation → Connecting to the world economy
☛ Key elements of globalisation → Free movement of trade, investment, technology, and labour
☛ Institution promoting globalisation → WTO (World Trade Organization)
☛ One benefit of globalisation → Technology transfer and economic development
☛ Major driver of globalisation → Multinational corporations (MNCs)
question_hi: आर्थिक शब्दों में वैश्वीकरण का मुख्य अर्थ क्या है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 1)

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है विश्व अर्थव्यवस्था से जुड़ना

Explanation:
आर्थिक वैश्वीकरण का अर्थ है विभिन्न देशों की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं का एकीकरण, जिसमें वस्तुओं, सेवाओं, पूंजी, प्रौद्योगिकी और श्रम का मुक्त प्रवाह शामिल है। यह सीमाओं के पार आर्थिक गतिविधियों को बढ़ावा देता है और व्यापार तथा निवेश में बाधाओं को कम करता है। वैश्वीकरण से देश एक-दूसरे पर निर्भर होते हैं, जिससे वैश्विक आपूर्ति श्रृंखलाएँ बनती हैं। इसके अंतर्गत विदेशी प्रत्यक्ष निवेश, बहुराष्ट्रीय कंपनियाँ और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय व्यापार बढ़ता है। विकासशील देशों को नई तकनीक और बाजारों तक पहुँच मिलती है, जबकि विकसित देशों को सस्ते श्रम और संसाधनों का लाभ होता है। इस प्रकार, वैश्वीकरण सीमाओं को बंद करने या व्यापार सीमित करने के विपरीत, आर्थिक एकीकरण को बढ़ावा देता है।

question: What was the major demographic feature of India at the time of independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: High life expectancy
High death rate and infant mortality
Aging population
Low birth rate
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is High death rate and infant mortality

Explanation:
At the time of independence, India's major demographic feature was high death rate and infant mortality. In 1947, life expectancy was around 32 years, much lower than today's 70 years. Infant mortality rate was over 200 per 1000 live births, indicating poor healthcare. Birth rate was high, but due to high death rate, population growth was slow. India was in the first stage of demographic transition, where death rates were high before later declining.

☛ India's life expectancy at independence → around 32 years
☛ Infant mortality rate in 1947 → over 200 per 1000 live births
☛ India's demographic transition model → entered second stage in the 1920s
☛ Main cause of high death rate → infectious diseases and malnutrition
☛ Literacy rate at independence → around 12%
question_hi: स्वतंत्रता के समय भारत की प्रमुख जनसांख्यिकीय विशेषता क्या थी? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 2)

उच्च मृत्यु दर और शिशु मृत्यु दर
वृद्ध होती जनसंख्या

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है उच्च मृत्यु दर और शिशु मृत्यु दर

Explanation:
स्वतंत्रता के समय भारत की जनसांख्यिकीय विशेषता उच्च मृत्यु दर और शिशु मृत्यु दर थी। 1947 में भारत की जीवन प्रत्याशा लगभग 32 वर्ष थी, जो आज के 70 वर्ष से बहुत कम थी। शिशु मृत्यु दर प्रति 1000 जीवित जन्मों पर 200 से अधिक थी, जो स्वास्थ्य सेवाओं की कमी को दर्शाता है। जन्म दर उच्च थी, लेकिन मृत्यु दर भी उच्च होने के कारण जनसंख्या वृद्धि धीमी थी। यह स्थिति प्रथम जनसांख्यिकीय संक्रमण के चरण में थी, जहाँ मृत्यु दर में गिरावट बाद में हुई।

question: Which of the following was NOT a component of globalisation in India's economic reforms? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Allowing foreign technology
Promoting local-only trade
Encouraging foreign direct investment
Liberalising imports
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Promoting local-only trade

Explanation:
In the 1991 economic reforms, globalisation meant integrating the Indian economy with the global market. Its components included allowing foreign technology, encouraging foreign direct investment (FDI), and liberalising imports, which increased international trade and investment. 'Promoting local-only trade' is opposite to globalisation, as it is a policy of closing the economy and prioritising domestic production, falling under protectionism. The aim of globalisation was to remove barriers, not restrict local trade.

question: What was one of the key effects of globalisation on the Indian economy after 1991? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Reduction in foreign exchange reserves
Entry of foreign companies and capital
Closure of Indian banks
Decrease in exports
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Entry of foreign companies and capital

Explanation:
After the 1991 economic reforms, India embraced globalisation, leading to a significant increase in the entry of foreign companies and capital. This was facilitated by liberalisation of foreign direct investment (FDI) and foreign portfolio investment (FPI) policies. As a result, the Indian economy gained access to advanced technology, managerial expertise, and new employment opportunities. Globalisation integrated Indian markets into the global supply chain, boosting both exports and imports. Consequently, foreign exchange reserves increased, rather than decreased, and Indian banks did not close. Thus, the most prominent effect was the influx of foreign companies and capital, which transformed India's economic landscape.

question: Which of the following is an example of globalisation in India post-1991? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (03/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Nationalisation of major private banks
Licensing requirement for all businesses
Entry of multinational companies like Amazon and Apple
Closure of ports
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Entry of multinational companies like Amazon and Apple

Explanation:
After the economic reforms of 1991, India embraced globalization by opening its economy to foreign investment and allowing multinational companies (MNCs) to enter. The entry of companies like Amazon and Apple is a clear example of globalization. Nationalisation of banks occurred in 1969 and 1980, unrelated to globalization. Licensing requirements were part of the pre-1991 industrial policy, abolished after reforms. Closure of ports contradicts globalization. Hence, the entry of MNCs is the correct example.

question: In 1947, the Indian economy was marked by deep poverty. Which sector dominated the Indian economy at the time of independence? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Agricultural sector
Industrial sector
Services sector
Manufacturing sector
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Agricultural sector

Explanation:
At the time of independence, the Indian economy was predominantly agricultural. Nearly 85% of the population lived in villages and over 70% of people depended on agriculture for their livelihood. Agriculture contributed more than 50% to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP). The industrial and service sectors were very small and underdeveloped. British rule used India as a source of raw materials and a market for finished goods, which hindered industrialization. The land system was exploitative and production techniques were outdated, leading to low agricultural productivity and widespread poverty.

question: What is the main aim of globalisation? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Limit foreign trade
Reduce employment
Increase local production
Integrate the Indian economy with the world
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Integrate the Indian economy with the world

Explanation:
The main aim of globalisation is to integrate different national economies into a single global market by reducing barriers to trade, investment, technology, and information flow. For India, globalisation focuses on integrating the Indian economy with the world economy, thereby promoting international trade and investment. This accelerates economic growth and facilitates the exchange of technology and knowledge. Limiting foreign trade or reducing employment contradicts the essence of globalisation. While increasing local production may be a positive outcome, it is not the primary objective of globalisation. The process aims at creating a more interconnected and interdependent global economy, benefiting participating countries through enhanced efficiency and access to global markets.

question: Which sector was the largest contributor to India's GDP between 1947 and 1991? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 2)

Agriculture sector
Industrial sector
Financial sector
solution:

Explanation:

question: What was the main focus of India’s Second Five Year Plan with respect to the economy? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (04/09/2025) Shift 3)
options: Heavy industrialisation
Expansion of services
Promotion of tourism
Green revolution
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Heavy industrialisation

Explanation:
The main focus of India's Second Five Year Plan (1956-61) was heavy industrialisation. This plan, also known as the Mahalanobis Model, aimed at developing capital goods industries to reduce import dependence and accelerate economic growth. Emphasis was placed on sectors like steel, coal, and electricity. The Green Revolution was the focus of the Third Five Year Plan (1961-66). Expansion of services and promotion of tourism were not the main priorities of this plan.

question: Which sector was most affected by liberalisation in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 1)
options: Public Distribution
Agriculture
Industry and Services
IT
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Industry and Services

Explanation:

This most significantly benefited the industry and services sector as privatisation, foreign competition, and technological advancements boosted growth. The IT sector emerged later but was not the most affected; the broader industrial and services sectors saw the greatest impact. Agriculture remained relatively less affected due to continued government controls. Liberalisation led to increased efficiency, foreign direct investment, and global integration for industries and services, making them the primary beneficiaries.

After economic reforms in 1991, India's trade was liberalized. Both exports and imports increased, but imports grew faster, especially in oil, machinery, and electronics. question: The British export-oriented strategy harmed the domestic economy. What impact did export-oriented policies have on India's food security? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Food shortages and famines occurred
Increased grain storage
Food prices decreased
Improved food availability
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Food shortages and famines occurred

Explanation:
Under the British export-oriented policies, excessive export of raw materials and food grains from India led to severe food shortages in the domestic market. Farmers were forced to grow cash crops, reducing food grain production. This policy resulted in frequent famines in India, such as the Great Famine of 1876-78 and the Bengal Famine of 1943. Millions died of starvation. Thus, this strategy severely damaged India's food security.

question: Globalization has increased cross-border flows of technology. What policy under globalization encourages technology transfer? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: Automatic route for FDI
Nationalisation
Import substitution policy
Licensing raj
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Automatic route for FDI

Explanation:
Under globalization, the automatic route for FDI is a policy that allows foreign investment without prior government approval, thereby encouraging technology transfer. It is part of liberalization and helps developing countries access advanced technology. In contrast, nationalisation (government control of industries), import substitution policy (focus on reducing imports), and licensing raj (extensive regulation) restrict technology flows. The automatic route permits foreign companies to invest without delays, bringing new technology and knowledge. This is a key aspect of globalization, promoting cross-border flows of technology and capital.

☛ What is meant by licensing raj? → Mandatory licenses for trade and investment
☛ Which policy is most important in globalization? → Liberalization and automatic FDI route

वैश्वीकरण के तहत FDI के लिए स्वचालित रूट एक ऐसी नीति है जो बिना सरकारी अनुमति के विदेशी निवेश की अनुमति देती है, जिससे प्रौद्योगिकी हस्तांतरण को बढ़ावा मिलता है। यह नीति उदारीकरण का हिस्सा है और विकासशील देशों को उन्नत तकनीक प्राप्त करने में मदद करती है। इसके विपरीत, राष्ट्रीयकरण (उद्योगों का सरकारी नियंत्रण), आयात प्रतिस्थापन नीति (आयात को कम करने पर केंद्रित), और लाइसेंसिंग राज (व्यापारिक नियंत्रण) प्रौद्योगिकी प्रवाह को सीमित करते हैं। स्वचालित रूट विदेशी कंपनियों को बिना देरी के निवेश करने की छूट देता है, जिससे नई तकनीक और ज्ञान देश में आता है। यह वैश्वीकरण का एक प्रमुख पहलू है।

☛ आयात प्रतिस्थापन नीति का मुख्य उद्देश्य क्या है? → स्वदेशी उद्योगों को संरक्षण देना

question: How has globalization helped India's exports? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)
options: without making any changes
by reducing it in
by banning it
by increasing exports to other countries
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is by increasing exports to other countries

Explanation:
Globalization has helped India's exports by reducing trade barriers and increasing access to international markets. It enabled Indian companies to integrate into global value chains, access technology and capital, and benefit from economies of scale. As a result, India's exports diversified, including services, manufacturing, and agricultural products. Globalization also facilitated free trade agreements with other countries, boosting export opportunities. Thus, it increased India's exports rather than reducing or banning them.

question_hi: वैश्वीकरण ने भारत के निर्यात में किस प्रकार सहायता की है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (08/09/2025) Shift 2)

इसमें में कमी करके
इस पर प्रतिबंध लगाके
अन्य देशों का निर्यात बढ़ाके
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अन्य देशों का निर्यात बढ़ाके

Explanation:
वैश्वीकरण ने व्यापार बाधाओं को कम करके और अंतर्राष्ट्रीय बाजारों तक पहुंच बढ़ाकर भारत के निर्यात को बढ़ावा दिया है। इसने भारतीय कंपनियों को वैश्विक मूल्य श्रृंखलाओं में एकीकृत होने, प्रौद्योगिकी और पूंजी तक पहुंच प्राप्त करने और पैमाने की अर्थव्यवस्थाओं से लाभ उठाने में सक्षम बनाया है। परिणामस्वरूप, भारत के निर्यात में विविधता आई है, जिसमें सेवाओं, विनिर्माण और कृषि उत्पादों का निर्यात शामिल है। वैश्वीकरण ने भारत को दूसरे देशों के साथ मुक्त व्यापार समझौते करने में भी मदद की है, जिससे निर्यात के अवसर बढ़े हैं। इसलिए, इसने भारत के निर्यात में वृद्धि की है।
